প্রজ্ঞাপন

তারিখ: ১৪ আষাঢ়, ১৪২৫ বঙ্গাব্দ/২৮ জুন, ২০১৮ খ্রিস্টাব্দ

এস. আর. ও. নং ২১৪-আইন/২০১৮/৩৭/কাস্টমস - Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 219, section 83E এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড নিম্নরূপ বিধিমালা প্রণয়ন করিল, যথা:-

Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the statutory authority under its various sections for the National Board of Revenue to formulate and issue customs-related rules and regulations.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is authorized to exercise its powers under specific sections of the Customs Act to establish and implement new rules and regulations.

১। সংক্ষিপ্ত শিরোনাম ও প্রবর্তন।— (১) এই বিধিমালা অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর (স্বীকৃতি প্রদান) বিধিমালা, ২০১৮ নামে অভিহিত হইবে।
(২) এই বিধিমালা অবিলম্বে কার্যকর হইবে।

Authorized Economic Operator (Licensing): This instrument is officially titled as the Authorized Economic Operator (Licensing) Rules 2018.
The rules shall come into immediate effect upon their issuance.

Authorized Economic Operator: An Authorized Economic Operator is defined as an entity that has received a recognition certificate from the Commissioner of Customs (Valuation and Internal Audit) under the relevant rules of this instrument.
Customs Act 1969: In this instrument, the term 'the Act' refers to the Customs Act 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969).
Application: An application is defined as a formal request submitted in the specified form as prescribed under the provisions of these rules.
Applicant: An applicant is defined as an economic operator engaged in customs-related activities who has submitted an application for the purpose of obtaining Authorized Economic Operator status.
Authorized Economic Operator Committee: The committee is defined as the specific body established under the rules to oversee matters related to Authorized Economic Operators.
Commissioner of Customs (Valuation and I: The Commissioner is defined as the officer holding the designation mentioned in the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969 regarding the Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate.
Officer of Customs: A customs officer is defined according to the meaning provided in the relevant definition section of the Customs Act 1969.
Form: The term form refers to any of the specific formats or documents prescribed within these rules.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue established under the National Board of Revenue Order, 1972.
Recognition Certificate: A recognition certificate is defined as the document issued under the sub-rules of this instrument granting formal recognition to an Authorized Economic Operator.

Authorized Economic Operator: A committee designated as the Authorized Economic Operator Committee is established to oversee and manage matters related to the Authorized Economic Operator program.

The committee is composed of several high-ranking customs officials, including a chairperson, the first secretary of the National Board of Revenue, and representatives from customs intelligence and investigation departments.
National Board of Revenue: The board is represented within the Authorized Economic Operator committee through the participation of its first secretary.
Customs Intelligence and Investigation D: The Director General of this directorate is responsible for nominating a senior official to serve as a member of the Authorized Economic Operator committee.
Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Com: This commissionerate provides necessary representation to the Authorized Economic Operator committee through officials nominated by the commissioner, including the member-secretary.

Authorized Economic Operator: The committee is responsible for scrutinizing applications for Authorized Economic Operator status.
The committee monitors the ongoing activities of Authorized Economic Operators and submits quarterly reports on these activities to the relevant member of the National Board of Revenue.
The committee provides recommendations regarding the issuance, suspension, or cancellation of accreditation certificates for these operators.
National Board of Revenue: The committee serves the National Board of Revenue by providing recommendations and submitting periodic monitoring reports concerning operator activities.
Monitoring Report: The committee is tasked with submitting quarterly reports to the relevant member of the National Board of Revenue regarding the operational performance and compliance of Authorized Economic Operators.

Authorized Economic Operator: This clause outlines the mandatory eligibility criteria for applicants seeking status as an Authorized Economic Operator.
Applicants must demonstrate a sustained period of business operation in Bangladesh, a clean compliance record with customs and tax laws, and a period of being free from proven offences.

Financial eligibility requirements include meeting specific thresholds for authorized capital, paid-up capital, or annual turnover, alongside requirements for average annual import or export volume based on the applicant's business category.

Applicants must maintain a satisfactory payment history for revenue duties and ensure that any penalties incurred in customs or tax matters within a specific prior period do not exceed a set percentage of the value of goods or services.

Application: Applicants must submit an application to the Commissioner using the prescribed Form-Ka along with all required supporting documentation.
The application must include a completed Self-Assessment Questionnaire and evidence supporting the information provided therein.
Form: Applicants are required to use Form-Ka for the submission of their application to the customs authorities.
Authorized Economic Operator: The Self-Assessment Questionnaire requires the business entity to provide extensive details on its organizational structure, financial status, internal control systems, and security procedures to qualify for recognition.
Failure to maintain adequate audit trails, internal controls, or security plans may result in the rejection of an application for recognition as an authorized economic operator by customs.
Business entities must document their procedures for managing customs formalities, securing premises, monitoring cargo, and conducting employee training to maintain eligibility.
Customs Procedure for Loading Goods: Business entities must establish formal procedures for managing the loading of goods, including clear allocation of responsibilities and supervision to prevent unauthorized access.
Entities are required to maintain records of loading processes, including seal numbers and completeness checks, and must have documented instructions to handle potential irregularities.

Application Processing: Every application received must be formally acknowledged by the relevant authority.
Each application must be presented to the committee in a separate file for review.
Self-Assessment Questionnaire: The information provided in the Self-Assessment Questionnaire must be verified through physical site inspection or audit.
Customs Audit: A dedicated audit team consisting of customs officers will be formed to verify the data provided by the applicant.
The audit team is required to submit a comprehensive report to the committee within a specified timeframe, subject to potential extensions granted by the committee chair.
Customs Committee: The committee is responsible for scrutinizing applications and submitted documents, requesting additional information from the applicant if necessary.
The committee evaluates the application alongside the audit report to form recommendations which are then submitted to the Commissioner of Customs.

Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is mandated to process applications within a specified maximum number of working days following the receipt of committee recommendations.
The Commissioner is responsible for issuing a recognition certificate in a prescribed format if an application is deemed acceptable based on committee recommendations.

Recognition Certificate: A recognition certificate is issued by the Commissioner of Customs in a specific prescribed format once an application has been reviewed and accepted based on committee recommendations.

processed_clauses.clause_title: অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর (AEO) এর প্রাপ্য সুবিধা

Authorized Economic Operator: Holders of the Authorized Economic Operator certification are entitled to various trade facilitation benefits to streamline their import and export processes.
Benefits include the option for physical examination of goods at the operator's own premises, expedited clearance or shipment, and access to dedicated customs teams for fast-track service.

Operators are granted the ability to process customs declarations prior to the arrival of goods, submit essential documents for clearance, and conduct communication with customs authorities through electronic means.
The operator may nominate representatives to receive special identification for easy access to customs stations, and the operator's business details will be published on the official customs website.
Additional support includes the prioritization of duty refunds and accelerated resolution of ongoing disputes through Alternative Dispute Resolution or other mechanisms.
Customs Physical Examination: Authorized Economic Operators are permitted to have goods physically examined at their own premises rather than at traditional customs houses or stations.
Alternative Dispute Resolution: The legal framework facilitates the expedited resolution of pending cases for Authorized Economic Operators through the use of Alternative Dispute Resolution.

Authorized Economic Operator: The committee is empowered to conduct audits on the activities of an Authorized Economic Operator.
These audits are scheduled to occur at least every three years, or at any other time deemed necessary by the committee.

Authorized Economic Operator: The member of the National Board of Revenue is authorized to establish a liaison group consisting of customs officials and private sector representatives to ensure the effective implementation of the Authorized Economic Operator program.
Liaison Group: This group is formed to oversee the implementation of the Authorized Economic Operator program and is responsible for providing recommendations regarding operational actions to the relevant board member within a specified timeframe.
National Board of Revenue: The board is empowered, through its designated member, to set the scope of work and structure for the liaison group tasked with supporting customs programs.

Authorized Economic Operator: The Commissioner has the authority to suspend or revoke the recognition certificate of an Authorized Economic Operator based on committee recommendations for specific violations such as providing false information, tax evasion, or failure to maintain eligibility requirements.
An Authorized Economic Operator may be granted a specified period to resolve certain types of complaints following the suspension of their certificate.

If an Authorized Economic Operator fails to resolve complaints within the allowed timeframe or is found guilty of duty evasion, the Commissioner may revoke their certificate after providing an opportunity for a hearing.
Once a certificate is revoked, the Authorized Economic Operator is prohibited from reapplying for a new certificate for a set number of years from the date of revocation.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner is empowered to suspend or revoke the recognition certificate of an Authorized Economic Operator upon the recommendation of a committee and following appropriate investigative procedures.

Authorized Economic Operator: An Authorized Economic Operator may file an appeal with the National Board of Revenue if aggrieved by an order issued by a Commissioner of Customs.

Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is the authority responsible for issuing orders that may be subject to an appeal process if a party is dissatisfied with the outcome.
